evidence.quote: MRCP was performed

MRCP demonstrated a thick-walled gallbladder containing multiple calculi, the largest measuring 2 cm (Figure 1). Appearances suggested a focal fundal perforation (Figure 2), with fluid extending beneath the hepatic capsule to form a 10 × 4 cm subcapsular collection. Associated findings included elevation of the right hemidiaphragm, right lower lobe collapse/consolidation, and a right pleural effusion. No intra- or extrahepatic duct dilatation or choledocholithiasis was seen. Multiple simple hepatic cysts were also noted. These findings raised suspicion for gallbladder perforation with subcapsular biloma.

An 87-year-old man presented with a four-day history of progressively worsening right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain, reduced appetite, one episode of vomiting, and dark urine. The pain was described as sharp, colicky, and similar to an episode of acute cholecystitis two months earlier, when he had been admitted, treated conservatively and listed for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Ultrasound assessment of the biloma initially found no safe drainage route due to diaphragmatic elevation. After discussion with interventional radiology, ultrasound-guided transhepatic drainage was ultimately performed under conscious sedation using the Seldinger technique. An 8Fr locking pigtail catheter was inserted, aspirating bile (culture negative) and confirming the diagnosis of biloma. There were no immediate complications.

summary.text: An 87-year-old man living independently with his wife, with hypertension, gallstones and regular amlodipine/omeprazole use, presented after four days of worsening sharp colicky RUQ pain with reduced appetite, one vomiting episode and dark urine. A conservatively treated cholecystitis admission two months earlier had led to elective surgery listing. He was tachypnoeic/hypoxic (RR 28, saturation 93% on 2 L), with Murphy’s sign, RUQ guarding and inspiratory referred shoulder-tip pain.

Admission WCC 11.5 ×10⁹/L, CRP 74 mg/L, ALT 145 U/L, ALP 301 U/L and bilirubin 59 µmol/L were recorded. IV co-amoxiclav was started. MRCP showed multiple gallstones (largest 2 cm), possible fundal perforation and a 10 ×4 cm hepatic subcapsular collection, with right hemidiaphragm elevation, right lower-lobe collapse/consolidation and right pleural effusion; duct dilatation and choledocholithiasis were not seen. Inflammatory markers worsened to CRP 316 mg/L/WCC 18.8 ×10⁹/L, and antibiotics were escalated to IV piperacillin-tazobactam.

After initial ultrasound found no safe route and discussion with interventional radiology, transhepatic Seldinger drainage under conscious sedation placed an 8Fr locking pigtail catheter. Aspirated bile confirmed biloma; culture was negative, with no immediate complications. Seven days later laparoscopic cholecystectomy and cholangiography confirmed fundal perforation, with adhesions and a slightly dilated CBD but no filling defects and free duodenal contrast flow. A 20F subhepatic drain was placed. He recovered well; subhepatic drain removal preceded next-day home discharge, radiological drain removal under fluoroscopy occurred three days later, and he remained well at undated follow-up.
